6.21.en: The Master said: The wise delight in water; the humane delight in mountains. The wise are active; the humane are still. The wise are joyful; the humane live long.
6.21.ja: 先生が言われた。知者は水を楽しみ、仁者は山を楽しむ。知者は動き、仁者は静か。知者は楽しみ、仁者は長生きする。

6.22.en: The Master said: With one change, Qi could reach the level of Lu; with one change, Lu could reach the Way.
6.22.ja: 先生が言われた。斉が一変すれば魯に至り、魯が一変すれば道に至る。

6.23.en: The Master said: A gu that is not a gu — a gu indeed! A gu indeed!
6.23.ja: 先生が言われた。觚が觚でなくなった。これが觚であろうか、これが觚であろうか。

6.24.en: Zai Wo asked: If a humane man were told, 'Someone humane has fallen into the well,' would he go in after him? The Master said: Why would he do that? A gentleman can be made to go there, but not to fall in; he can be deceived, but not fooled into folly.
6.24.ja: 宰我が問うた。仁者は、井戸に人が落ちたと告げられたら、後を追って飛び込むのでしょうか。先生「どうしてそんなことをしようか。君子は行かせることはできても、落とし入れることはできない。欺くことはできても、道理に外れたことでだますことはできない。」

6.25.en: The Master said: A gentleman who learns broadly in culture and restrains it with ritual may thereby avoid going astray.
6.25.ja: 先生が言われた。君子が広く文を学び、礼でそれを締めくくれば、道に背かずにいられるだろう。

6.26.en: The Master went to see Nanzi, and Zilu was displeased. The Master swore: If I have done wrong, may Heaven reject me! May Heaven reject me!
6.26.ja: 先生が南子に会われ、子路は不満であった。先生は誓って言われた。「私に間違ったところがあれば、天が見捨てるだろう。天が見捨てるだろう。」

6.27.en: The Master said: As a virtue, the constant mean is the highest of all! Yet it has long been rare among the people.
6.27.ja: 先生が言われた。中庸という徳は、この上ないものだ。民の間でそれが乏しくなって久しい。

6.28.en: Zigong said: If someone gave widely to the people and could relieve the multitude, what would you say? Could he be called humane? The Master said: Why stop at humane? He would surely be a sage! Even Yao and Shun found this hard. The humane man, wishing to stand, helps others stand; wishing to reach, helps others reach. To take what is near as an example — this may be called the method of humaneness.
6.28.ja: 子貢が言った。「広く民に施し、多くの人を救える者がいたら、どうでしょう。仁と言えますか。」先生「仁どころではない、聖であろう。堯・舜でさえ難しいとされた。仁者は、自分が立ちたければ人を立たせ、自分が達したければ人を達させる。身近なところに例を取れること、それが仁の方法といえる。」

7.1.en: The Master said: I transmit and do not create; I trust and love antiquity. I venture to compare myself to our Old Peng.
7.1.ja: 先生が言われた。述べて作らず、信じて古を好む。ひそかに我が老彭に比べている。

7.2.en: The Master said: To store things silently in mind, to learn without tiring, to teach others without weariness — which of these is in me?
7.2.ja: 先生が言われた。黙って覚え、学んで飽きず、人を教えて倦まない。このうち何が私にあろうか。

7.3.en: The Master said: Virtue not cultivated, learning not discussed, hearing what is right yet not moving toward it, having faults yet not correcting them — these are my worries.
7.3.ja: 先生が言われた。徳を修めず、学を講じず、義を聞いても移れず、不善を改められない。これが私の憂いである。

7.4.en: At leisure at home, the Master was relaxed and easy, cheerful and at ease.
7.4.ja: 先生がくつろいでおられるときは、のびのびとして、にこやかであった。

7.5.en: The Master said: How far I have declined! It has been long since I last saw the Duke of Zhou in my dreams.
7.5.ja: 先生が言われた。ひどいものだ、私の衰えは。久しく周公を夢に見なくなった。

7.6.en: The Master said: Set your will on the Way, hold to virtue, rely on humaneness, and roam in the arts.
7.6.ja: 先生が言われた。道に志し、徳に拠り、仁に依り、芸に遊ぶ。

7.7.en: The Master said: From anyone who brought a bundle of dried meat or more, I never withheld instruction.
7.7.ja: 先生が言われた。束脩を持ってきた者から上は、私は教えなかったことがない。

7.8.en: The Master said: I do not open the way for one who is not eager, nor help out one who is not struggling to speak. If I show one corner and he cannot come back with the other three, I do not repeat myself.
7.8.ja: 先生が言われた。憤らなければ啓かず、悱えなければ発しない。一隅を挙げて三隅で返してこなければ、繰り返さない。

7.9.en: When the Master ate beside someone in mourning, he never ate his fill. On a day when he had wept, he did not sing.
7.9.ja: 先生は喪中の人のそばで食事をされるとき、満腹まで食べることはなかった。その日に哭されたときは、歌わなかった。

7.10.en: The Master said to Yan Yuan: When employed, act; when set aside, withdraw — only you and I are like this. Zilu said: If you led the three armies, whom would you take with you? The Master said: One who would fight a tiger bare-handed or ford a river on foot, dying without regret — him I would not take. It must be someone who approaches affairs with caution and likes to plan and succeed.
7.10.ja: 先生が顔淵に言われた。「用いられれば行い、捨てられれば隠れる。これができるのは私とお前だけだな。」子路「先生が三軍を率いるなら、誰と一緒になさいますか。」先生「素手で虎に挑み、歩いて河を渡り、死んでも悔いない者とは組まない。事に臨んで慎重で、よく謀って成し遂げる者とだ。」

7.11.en: The Master said: If wealth could be sought, I would do it even as a man holding the whip. If it cannot be sought, I follow what I love.
7.11.ja: 先生が言われた。富が求めて得られるものなら、鞭を執る役人でもやろう。求めて得られないなら、自分の好むことに従う。

7.12.en: The things the Master was careful about: fasting, war, and illness.
7.12.ja: 先生が慎まれたのは、斎戒・戦争・病気であった。

7.13.en: In Qi the Master heard the Shao music, and for three months did not know the taste of meat. He said: I never imagined music could reach such heights!
7.13.ja: 先生は斉で韶の楽を聞き、三か月の間、肉の味がわからなかった。「音楽がここまでのものになるとは思わなかった。」

7.14.en: Ran You said: Is our Master on the side of the ruler of Wei? Zigong said: Well, I will ask him. He went in and said: What sort of men were Boyi and Shuqi? The Master said: Worthy men of old. Did they feel resentment? They sought humaneness and attained it; what was there to resent? Zigong came out and said: The Master is not on his side.
7.14.ja: 冉有が言った。「先生は衛の君に味方なさるだろうか。」子貢「よし、聞いてみよう。」入って言った。「伯夷・叔斉はどういう人ですか。」「古の賢人だ。」「恨みましたか。」「仁を求めて仁を得たのだ、何を恨もう。」出てきて言った。「先生は味方なさらない。」

7.15.en: The Master said: Eating coarse food and drinking water, bending my arm for a pillow — there is joy in this too. Wealth and rank gained unjustly are to me like floating clouds.
7.15.ja: 先生が言われた。粗末な飯を食べ水を飲み、肘を曲げて枕にする。楽しみはその中にもある。不義で得た富貴は、私にとって浮雲のようなものだ。

7.16.en: The Master said: Give me a few more years, and if I could study the Changes at fifty, I might be free of great faults.
7.16.ja: 先生が言われた。私にあと数年を与えて、五十で易を学ばせてくれれば、大きな過ちはなくなるだろう。

7.17.en: What the Master spoke in the standard pronunciation: the Odes, the Documents, and the conduct of ritual — all in the standard speech.
7.17.ja: 先生が雅言で語られたのは、詩・書と礼を執り行うときで、みな雅言であった。

7.18.en: The Duke of She asked Zilu about Confucius, and Zilu did not answer. The Master said: Why did you not say: He is the kind of man who forgets to eat in his eagerness, forgets his worries in his joy, and does not notice that old age is coming?
7.18.ja: 葉公が子路に孔子のことを尋ねたが、子路は答えなかった。先生「なぜ言わなかったのか。その人となりは、発憤して食を忘れ、楽しんで憂いを忘れ、老いが来るのにも気づかない、と。」

7.19.en: The Master said: I was not born knowing. I love antiquity and am quick to seek it out.
7.19.ja: 先生が言われた。私は生まれながらに知る者ではない。古を好み、努めて求める者だ。

7.20.en: The Master did not speak of the strange, of force, of disorder, or of spirits.
7.20.ja: 先生は怪・力・乱・神を語らなかった。

7.21.en: The Master said: When three walk together, there is surely a teacher for me among them. I pick out the good and follow it; the not-good I correct in myself.
7.21.ja: 先生が言われた。三人で行けば、必ず私の師がいる。善いところを選んで従い、善くないところは自分を改める。

7.22.en: The Master said: Heaven gave birth to the virtue in me; what can Huan Tui do to me?
7.22.ja: 先生が言われた。天が私に徳を生じたのだ。桓魋ごときが私をどうできよう。

7.23.en: The Master said: You, my disciples, think I am hiding something? I hide nothing from you. There is nothing I do that I do not share with you — that is who I am.
7.23.ja: 先生が言われた。諸君は私が隠しごとをしていると思うか。私は何も隠していない。私の行いで諸君に示さないものはない。それが私だ。

7.24.en: The Master taught four things: culture, conduct, loyalty, and good faith.
7.24.ja: 先生は四つのことで教えられた。文・行・忠・信である。

7.25.en: The Master said: A sage I cannot hope to see; if I could see a gentleman, that would be enough. The Master said: A good man I cannot hope to see; if I could see someone constant, that would be enough. Having nothing yet acting as if one has, being empty yet acting full, being straitened yet acting at ease — it is hard for such a one to be constant.
7.25.ja: 先生が言われた。聖人には会えない。君子に会えればそれでよい。先生が言われた。善人には会えない。恒心のある者に会えればそれでよい。無いのに有るふりをし、空なのに満ちたふりをし、乏しいのにゆとりあるふりをする。これでは恒心を保つのは難しい。

7.26.en: The Master fished with a line but not with a net; he shot birds with a corded arrow, but not birds at roost.
7.26.ja: 先生は釣りはしても網は使わず、いぐるみで射ても、ねぐらの鳥は射なかった。

7.27.en: The Master said: There may be those who act without knowing; I am not one of them. I hear much, choose the good and follow it; I see much and remember it. This is the next best to knowing.
7.27.ja: 先生が言われた。知らずに作る者もいるだろうが、私はそうではない。多く聞いて善いものを選んで従い、多く見て覚える。これは知るに次ぐものだ。

7.28.en: The people of Huxiang were hard to talk with. A boy from there came to see the Master, and the disciples were puzzled. The Master said: I approve of his coming forward, not of his going back. Why be so severe? When a person purifies himself to come forward, I approve of that purity; I do not vouch for his past.
7.28.ja: 互郷の人は話しにくかった。そこの少年が会いに来て、門人は戸惑った。先生「進んで来たことを認めるのであって、退くことを認めるのではない。何をそんなに厳しくするのか。人が身を清めて進んで来たなら、その清さを認める。過去までは保証しない。」

7.29.en: The Master said: Is humaneness far away? I wish for humaneness, and here humaneness is.
7.29.ja: 先生が言われた。仁は遠いものだろうか。私が仁を欲すれば、仁はすぐにやって来る。

7.30.en: The Minister of Crime of Chen asked whether Duke Zhao knew ritual. Confucius said: He knew ritual. After Confucius withdrew, the minister bowed Wuma Qi forward and said: I have heard that a gentleman is not partial; is a gentleman partial after all? Your lord married a woman of Wu of the same surname and called her Wu Mengzi. If your lord knew ritual, who does not know ritual? Wuma Qi reported this. The Master said: I am fortunate. If I make a mistake, others are sure to know it.
7.30.ja: 陳の司敗が問うた。「昭公は礼を知っていましたか。」孔子「知っていた。」孔子が退くと、司敗は巫馬期に会釈して進ませ、言った。「君子は党しないと聞くが、君子も党するのか。君は呉から同姓の妻を娶り、呉孟子と呼んだ。君が礼を知っているなら、誰が礼を知らないというのか。」巫馬期がこれを告げた。先生「私は幸せだ。過ちがあれば、人が必ず気づいてくれる。」

7.31.en: When the Master sang with others and someone sang well, he would have him repeat it, and then join in.
7.31.ja: 先生は人と歌って、その人がうまければ、必ずもう一度歌わせ、それから唱和された。

7.32.en: The Master said: In learning I may be no worse than others. But as for living as a gentleman in my own conduct, that I have not yet attained.
7.32.ja: 先生が言われた。学問なら私も人並みだろう。だが君子として身をもって行うことは、まだできていない。

7.33.en: The Master said: As for sagehood and humaneness, how would I dare? But working at them without tiring and teaching others without weariness — that much may be said of me. Gongxi Hua said: That is exactly what we disciples cannot learn.
7.33.ja: 先生が言われた。聖と仁など、どうしてあえて名乗れよう。ただ、それを行って飽きず、人に教えて倦まない、とは言えるだろう。公西華「それこそ私たち弟子が学べないところです。」

7.34.en: The Master was gravely ill, and Zilu asked to offer prayers. The Master said: Is there such a thing? Zilu replied: There is. The eulogy says: We pray for you to the spirits above and below. The Master said: My praying has gone on for a long time.
7.34.ja: 先生の病が重く、子路が祈ることを願い出た。先生「そういうことがあるのか。」子路「あります。誄に『汝を上下の神祇に祈る』とあります。」先生「私の祈りは久しいものだ。」

7.35.en: The Master said: Extravagance leads to arrogance; frugality leads to shabbiness. Rather than be arrogant, better to be shabby.
7.35.ja: 先生が言われた。贅沢だと不遜になり、倹約だと頑なになる。不遜であるよりは、むしろ頑なであれ。

7.36.en: The Master said: The gentleman is open and at ease; the petty man is always anxious and distressed.
7.36.ja: 先生が言われた。君子は心が平らでのびやか、小人はいつもくよくよしている。

7.37.en: The Master was gentle yet stern, commanding yet not fierce, respectful yet at ease.
7.37.ja: 先生は温和でいて厳しく、威厳があっても猛々しくなく、恭しくて安らかであった。

8.1.en: The Master said: Taibo may be called a man of the highest virtue! Three times he declined the realm, and the people could find no words to praise him.
8.1.ja: 先生が言われた。泰伯こそ至徳と言えよう。三たび天下を譲ったが、民はそれをたたえる言葉も見いだせなかった。

8.2.en: The Master said: Respect without ritual becomes toil; caution without ritual becomes timidity; courage without ritual becomes disorder; straightness without ritual becomes harshness. When the gentleman is devoted to his kin, the people rise to humaneness; when old friends are not forgotten, the people are not cold.
8.2.ja: 先生が言われた。恭しくても礼がなければ疲れ、慎重でも礼がなければ臆病になり、勇敢でも礼がなければ乱れ、まっすぐでも礼がなければ窮屈になる。君子が親族に厚ければ民は仁に興り、古なじみを忘れなければ民は薄情にならない。

8.3.en: Zengzi was ill and called his disciples: Uncover my feet! Uncover my hands! The Odes say: 'Fearful and careful, as if near a deep abyss, as if treading thin ice.' From now on, I know I am spared, my young friends!
8.3.ja: 曾子が病気になり、門弟を呼んで言った。「私の足を開いて見よ、手を開いて見よ。詩に『戦戦兢兢として、深淵に臨むが如く、薄氷を履むが如し』とある。これから先は、私も免れたとわかる。諸君よ。」

8.4.en: Zengzi was ill and Meng Jingzi came to ask after him. Zengzi said: When a bird is about to die, its cry is mournful; when a man is about to die, his words are good. There are three things in the Way that a gentleman values: in his bearing, he keeps far from violence and insolence; in setting his countenance, he comes near to good faith; in his words and tone, he keeps far from vulgarity and impropriety. As for the matters of ritual vessels, there are officers for that.
8.4.ja: 曾子が病気になり、孟敬子が見舞った。曾子は言った。「鳥が死のうとするとき、その鳴き声は哀しい。人が死のうとするとき、その言葉は善い。君子が道において大切にするのは三つ。容貌を動かすときは乱暴や傲慢から遠ざかり、顔色を正すときは誠に近づき、言葉を出すときは卑しさや道理に背くことから遠ざかる。祭器のことは係の役人がいる。」

8.5.en: Zengzi said: Able, yet asking those less able; knowing much, yet asking those who know little; having, as if not having; full, as if empty; wronged, yet not retaliating — once I had a friend who lived this way.
8.5.ja: 曾子が言った。能力がありながら能力のない者に問い、多く知りながら少なく知る者に問い、有っても無いかのように、満ちていても空であるかのようにし、害されても仕返ししない。昔、私の友はこういうことに努めていた。

8.6.en: Zengzi said: One who can be entrusted with an orphaned young ruler, who can be given charge of a state of a hundred li, and who in a great crisis cannot be swayed — is he a gentleman? He is a gentleman.
8.6.ja: 曾子が言った。幼い君主を託すことができ、百里の国の命運を預けることができ、大事に臨んでも志を奪われない。君子の人であろうか。君子の人である。

8.7.en: Zengzi said: A scholar must be broad and resolute, for his burden is heavy and his road is long. He takes humaneness as his burden — is that not heavy? It ends only with death — is that not long?
8.7.ja: 曾子が言った。士は度量が広く意志が強くなければならない。任は重く道は遠い。仁を自分の任とする、重くないだろうか。死んでやっと終わる、遠くないだろうか。

8.8.en: The Master said: Be roused by the Odes, be established by ritual, be completed by music.
8.8.ja: 先生が言われた。詩に興り、礼に立ち、楽に成る。

8.9.en: The Master said: The people can be made to follow it, but cannot be made to understand it.
8.9.ja: 先生が言われた。民は従わせることはできるが、理由をわからせることはできない。

8.10.en: The Master said: One who loves daring and hates poverty will make trouble. A man who is not humane, if hated too much, will make trouble.
8.10.ja: 先生が言われた。勇を好んで貧しさを嫌えば、乱を起こす。不仁の人を憎みすぎれば、これも乱を起こす。

8.11.en: The Master said: Even with the talents and fine qualities of the Duke of Zhou, if a man were arrogant and stingy, the rest would not be worth looking at.
8.11.ja: 先生が言われた。周公ほどの才能の美しさがあっても、驕って吝嗇なら、残りは見るに足りない。

8.12.en: The Master said: One who studies for three years without aiming at a salary is not easy to find.
8.12.ja: 先生が言われた。三年学んで俸禄を志さない者は、なかなか得がたい。

8.13.en: The Master said: Hold firmly to good faith and love learning; guard the good Way unto death. Do not enter a state in danger; do not live in a state in disorder. When the realm has the Way, show yourself; when it lacks the Way, stay hidden. When the state has the Way, to be poor and lowly is shameful; when the state lacks the Way, to be rich and honored is shameful.
8.13.ja: 先生が言われた。篤く信じて学を好み、死を守って道を善くする。危うい国には入らず、乱れた国には住まない。天下に道があれば現れ、なければ隠れる。国に道があるのに貧しく賤しいのは恥であり、国に道がないのに富み貴いのも恥である。

8.14.en: The Master said: When not in the office, do not plan its affairs.
8.14.ja: 先生が言われた。その地位にいなければ、その政を謀らない。

8.15.en: The Master said: From Music Master Zhi's opening to the finale of the Guanju — how full and flowing it fills the ears!
8.15.ja: 先生が言われた。楽師摯の始まりから関雎の終章まで、豊かに耳に満ちることよ。

8.16.en: The Master said: Wild yet not straight, ignorant yet not honest, simple yet not trustworthy — such people I do not understand.
8.16.ja: 先生が言われた。気負っていて率直でなく、無知で実直でなく、愚直で誠実でない。そういう者は私にはわからない。

8.17.en: The Master said: Learn as if you could not catch up, and still fear losing it.
8.17.ja: 先生が言われた。学ぶときは追いつけないかのようにし、それでもなお失うのを恐れる。

8.18.en: The Master said: How lofty! Shun and Yu possessed the realm, yet did not make it their concern.
8.18.ja: 先生が言われた。高大なことよ。舜と禹は天下を保ちながら、それに関わろうとしなかった。

8.19.en: The Master said: Great indeed was Yao as a ruler! How lofty! Only Heaven is great, and only Yao modeled himself on it. How vast! The people could find no name for it. How lofty were his achievements! How brilliant his culture!
8.19.ja: 先生が言われた。偉大なことよ、堯の君としてのありようは。高大なことよ、ただ天だけが大きく、ただ堯だけがそれに則った。広大なことよ、民はそれを名づけようがなかった。高大なことよ、その成し遂げた功績は。輝かしいことよ、その文化は。

8.20.en: Shun had five ministers and the realm was well governed. King Wu said: I have ten ministers who keep order. Confucius said: Talent is hard to find — is it not so? From the time of Tang and Yu, it flourished most in this age; and one of them was a woman, so there were only nine men. Holding two thirds of the realm, Zhou still served Yin. The virtue of Zhou may be called the highest virtue.
8.20.ja: 舜には臣が五人いて天下が治まった。武王は言った。「私には治める臣が十人いる。」孔子が言われた。「人材は得がたいというが、その通りではないか。唐・虞の時代以後、この時が最も盛んであった。それでも女性が一人いて、男は九人だけだ。天下の三分の二を有しながら殷に仕えた。周の徳は至徳と言えよう。」

8.21.en: The Master said: In Yu I find no fault. He ate and drank simply, yet was utterly devoted to the spirits; he wore poor clothes, yet made his ceremonial robes and cap beautiful; he lived in a low palace, yet gave all his strength to the irrigation channels. In Yu I find no fault.
8.21.ja: 先生が言われた。禹には非の打ちどころがない。飲食を質素にして鬼神には孝を尽くし、衣服を粗末にして祭服や冠は美しくし、宮室を低くして水路には力を尽くした。禹には非の打ちどころがない。

9.1.en: The Master seldom spoke of profit, of fate, or of humaneness.
9.1.ja: 先生は利と命と仁について、まれにしか語らなかった。

9.2.en: A man of Daxiang village said: Great indeed is Confucius! He has learned so broadly, yet made no name in any one thing. Hearing this, the Master said to his disciples: What should I take up? Charioteering? Archery? I will take up charioteering.
9.2.ja: 達巷の村人が言った。「偉大だ、孔子は。博く学んで、一つのことで名を成したものがない。」先生はこれを聞いて門弟に言われた。「私は何を専門にしようか。御者をしようか、弓を射ようか。御者にしよう。」

9.3.en: The Master said: A linen cap is the ritual; now silk is used, which is more frugal, and I follow the majority. Bowing below the hall is the ritual; now people bow above it, which is presumptuous. Though it goes against the majority, I bow below.
9.3.ja: 先生が言われた。麻の冠が礼である。今は絹を用いるが、倹約なので私も皆に従う。堂の下で拝するのが礼である。今は堂の上で拝するが、驕りである。皆に背いても、私は下で拝する。

9.4.en: The Master was free of four things: no presumption, no insistence, no stubbornness, no self.
9.4.ja: 先生は四つのことを絶っておられた。意なく、必なく、固なく、我なし。

9.5.en: The Master was in peril in Kuang. He said: Since King Wen is gone, is culture not here in me? If Heaven meant to destroy this culture, those who came after would not have shared in it. If Heaven does not mean to destroy this culture, what can the people of Kuang do to me?
9.5.ja: 先生が匡で危難にあわれた。「文王はすでに亡いが、文はここにあるではないか。天がこの文を滅ぼすつもりなら、後の者がこの文に与ることはなかったはずだ。天がまだこの文を滅ぼさないなら、匡の人が私をどうできよう。」

9.6.en: The Grand Steward asked Zigong: Is your Master a sage? How many skills he has! Zigong said: Heaven has indeed endowed him to be nearly a sage, and he has many skills as well. Hearing this, the Master said: Does the Grand Steward know me? When young I was of low station, so I became skilled in many humble things. Does a gentleman need many skills? Not many. Lao said: The Master said, 'I was not given office, so I learned the arts.'
9.6.ja: 大宰が子貢に問うた。「先生は聖者でしょうか。なんと多能なことか。」子貢「もとより天が聖人たらしめようとしたうえに、多能でもあるのです。」先生はこれを聞いて言われた。「大宰は私を知っているのか。私は若いころ身分が低かったので、つまらないことが多くできるのだ。君子は多能だろうか、多くはない。」牢が言った。「先生は『用いられなかったから芸を身につけた』とおっしゃった。」

9.7.en: The Master said: Do I have knowledge? I do not. If a common man asks me something, and I am completely empty, I lay out both ends of the matter and exhaust it.
9.7.ja: 先生が言われた。私に知があるだろうか。ない。つまらない男が私に問うて、空っぽであっても、私はその両端を叩いて尽くすのだ。

9.8.en: The Master said: The phoenix does not come, the River gives forth no chart. It is all over with me!
9.8.ja: 先生が言われた。鳳凰は来ず、黄河から図は出ない。私はもうおしまいだ。

9.9.en: When the Master saw someone in mourning dress, someone in ceremonial cap and robes, or a blind man, he would rise on seeing them, even if they were young; passing them, he would quicken his step.
9.9.ja: 先生は喪服の人、冠と礼服の人、目の見えない人を見ると、相手が若くても必ず立ち上がり、前を通るときは必ず小走りになった。

9.10.en: Yan Yuan sighed deeply and said: The more I look up to it, the higher it is; the more I bore into it, the harder it is. I see it before me, and suddenly it is behind. The Master leads people on step by step; he broadens me with culture and restrains me with ritual. I want to stop but cannot. When I have used up all my ability, it seems to stand there, towering. Though I want to follow it, there is no way.
9.10.ja: 顔淵がため息をついて言った。「仰げばいよいよ高く、鑽ればいよいよ堅い。前にあるかと見れば、たちまち後ろにある。先生は順序立ててうまく人を導き、文で私を広め、礼で私を締めくくる。やめようとしてもやめられない。才を尽くしても、そびえ立つものがあるようで、従おうとしても、どうしようもない。」

9.11.en: The Master was gravely ill, and Zilu had disciples act as his retainers. When the illness eased, the Master said: How long Zilu has been practicing this deceit! I have no retainers, yet he acts as if I do. Whom am I deceiving? Am I deceiving Heaven? Besides, rather than die in the hands of retainers, would I not rather die in your hands, my friends? And even if I am not given a grand burial, would I die by the roadside?
9.11.ja: 先生の病が重く、子路は門人を家臣に仕立てた。病が少しよくなると、先生は言われた。「久しいことだな、由の偽りは。家臣がいないのにいるようにする。私は誰を欺くのか。天を欺くのか。それに私は家臣の手で死ぬよりは、諸君の手で死にたい。立派な葬式をしてもらえなくても、道端で死ぬわけではあるまい。」

9.12.en: Zigong said: Here is a beautiful jade. Should one store it away in a case, or seek a good price and sell it? The Master said: Sell it! Sell it! I am waiting for the right price.
9.12.ja: 子貢が言った。「ここに美しい玉があります。箱に納めてしまっておきますか、よい買い手を求めて売りますか。」先生「売ろう、売ろう。私は買い手を待っているのだ。」

9.13.en: The Master wished to live among the nine Yi tribes. Someone said: They are crude; what would you do? The Master said: If a gentleman lived there, what crudeness would there be?
9.13.ja: 先生が九夷に住もうとされた。ある人が「むさくるしいところです、どうなさいます」と言った。先生「君子が住めば、何のむさくるしいことがあろう。」

9.14.en: The Master said: Only after I returned from Wei to Lu was the music set right, and the Ya and Song each found their proper place.
9.14.ja: 先生が言われた。私が衛から魯に帰ってから、音楽が正され、雅と頌がそれぞれ正しい所を得た。

9.15.en: The Master said: Abroad, serving dukes and ministers; at home, serving father and elder brothers; in mourning, never daring not to do my utmost; never being overcome by wine — which of these is in me?
9.15.ja: 先生が言われた。外では公卿に仕え、家では父兄に仕え、喪事には努めないことがなく、酒に乱されない。このうち何が私にあろうか。

9.16.en: Standing by a river, the Master said: It flows on like this, never ceasing day or night.
9.16.ja: 先生が川のほとりで言われた。過ぎゆくものはこの水のようだ。昼も夜も休むことがない。

9.17.en: The Master said: I have never seen anyone who loves virtue as much as he loves beauty.
9.17.ja: 先生が言われた。色を好むように徳を好む者を、私はまだ見たことがない。

9.18.en: The Master said: It is like building a mound: if I stop when it lacks only one basket of earth, it is I who stop. It is like leveling the ground: even if I have tipped out only one basket, if I go on, it is I who go forward.
9.18.ja: 先生が言われた。たとえば山を築くのに、あと一もっこで完成というところで止めるのも、私が止めるのだ。たとえば地をならすのに、一もっこあけただけでも、進むのは私が進むのだ。

9.19.en: The Master said: One who never grew lax when I spoke to him — that was Hui!
9.19.ja: 先生が言われた。話してやって怠らなかったのは、回であろうか。

9.20.en: Speaking of Yan Yuan, the Master said: What a pity! I saw him go forward; I never saw him stop.
9.20.ja: 先生が顔淵について言われた。惜しいことだ。私は彼が進むのを見たが、止まるのを見たことがなかった。

9.21.en: The Master said: There are sprouts that never flower! There are flowers that never bear fruit!
9.21.ja: 先生が言われた。苗のまま穂を出さないものがあるな。穂を出しても実らないものがあるな。

9.22.en: The Master said: The young are to be held in awe. How do we know those to come will not equal those of today? But one who at forty or fifty has made no name — he is not worth holding in awe.
9.22.ja: 先生が言われた。後生畏るべし。これから来る者が今の者に及ばないと、どうしてわかろう。だが四十、五十になって評判が聞こえないなら、畏れるに足りない。

9.23.en: The Master said: Words of correction — can one fail to accept them? What matters is to change. Words of gentle advice — can one fail to be pleased? What matters is to think them through. Pleased but not thinking it through, accepting but not changing — with such a person I can do nothing.
9.23.ja: 先生が言われた。正しい言葉で諭されれば、従わずにいられようか。改めることが大切だ。穏やかな言葉で導かれれば、喜ばずにいられようか。その意味をたずねることが大切だ。喜んでもたずねず、従っても改めないなら、私にはどうしようもない。

9.24.en: The Master said: Hold loyalty and good faith as primary. Do not befriend those not your equal. When you err, do not fear to correct it.
9.24.ja: 先生が言われた。忠信を主とし、自分に及ばない者を友とするな。過ちがあれば改めるのをためらうな。

9.25.en: The Master said: The three armies can be robbed of their commander; a common man cannot be robbed of his will.
9.25.ja: 先生が言われた。三軍もその大将を奪うことはできるが、一人の男もその志を奪うことはできない。

9.26.en: The Master said: Wearing a tattered padded robe and standing beside men in fox and badger furs without shame — that would be You, would it not? 'Not envious, not grasping — how could he not be good?' Zilu kept reciting these lines all his life. The Master said: That way alone — how is it enough to be good?
9.26.ja: 先生が言われた。破れた綿入れを着て、狐や貉の毛皮を着た者と並んで立っても恥じないのは、由であろうか。「ねたまず求めず、どうして善くないことがあろう。」子路は生涯これを口ずさんでいた。先生「その道だけで、どうして善いと言えよう。」

9.27.en: The Master said: Only when the year turns cold do we know that the pine and cypress are the last to wither.
9.27.ja: 先生が言われた。寒さが厳しくなって、はじめて松や柏が最後まで凋まないことがわかる。

9.28.en: The Master said: The wise are not perplexed; the humane are not anxious; the brave are not afraid.
9.28.ja: 先生が言われた。知者は惑わず、仁者は憂えず、勇者は懼れない。

9.29.en: The Master said: Some you can study with, but not go with toward the Way; some you can go with toward the Way, but not stand with; some you can stand with, but not weigh things with.
9.29.ja: 先生が言われた。共に学ぶことはできても、共に道に進むことはできない者がいる。共に道に進めても、共に立つことはできない者がいる。共に立てても、共に権ることはできない者がいる。

9.30.en: 'The blossoms of the cherry tree flutter and turn. How could I not think of you? But your home is far away.' The Master said: He did not really think of her. What distance would there be?
9.30.ja: 「唐棣の花、ひらひらと翻る。あなたを思わないではないが、家が遠いのだ。」先生が言われた。本当には思っていないのだ。思えば何の遠いことがあろう。

10.1.en: In his home village, Confucius was simple and sincere, as if unable to speak. In the ancestral temple and at court, he spoke fluently, but always with care.
10.1.ja: 孔子は郷里では、慎み深く、ものも言えない人のようであった。宗廟や朝廷では、はっきりと話したが、ただ慎重であった。

10.2.en: At court, speaking with lower officers, he was direct and at ease; speaking with higher officers, he was respectful and exact. When the ruler was present, he was reverent yet composed.
10.2.ja: 朝廷で下大夫と話すときは和やかに率直で、上大夫と話すときは慎み深く正しかった。君主がおられるときは、恭しくかしこまりながら、ゆったりと落ち着いていた。

10.3.en: When the ruler summoned him to receive guests, his face would change and his steps would quicken. Bowing to those standing beside him, he moved his hands left and right, his robe swaying evenly front and back. Hurrying forward, he moved like a bird with spread wings. When the guest had left, he would report: The guest is no longer looking back.
10.3.ja: 君主に呼ばれて賓客の接待役を命じられると、顔色を改め、足取りは慎重になった。共に立つ人に会釈して左右に手を動かすと、衣の前後がきちんと整っていた。小走りに進むときは、翼を広げたようであった。賓客が帰ると、必ず「客はもう振り返りません」と復命した。

10.4.en: Entering the palace gate, he bowed as if there were no room for him. He did not stand in the middle of the gateway nor step on the threshold. Passing the ruler's seat, his face changed and his steps quickened, and he spoke as if short of words. Lifting his robe to ascend the hall, he bowed and held his breath as if not breathing. Coming out and descending one step, he relaxed his face and looked at ease. At the bottom of the steps he hurried forward like a bird with spread wings. Returning to his place, he was reverent and composed.
10.4.ja: 宮門を入るときは、身をかがめて、入りきれないかのようにした。門の中央に立たず、敷居を踏まなかった。君主の席の前を通るときは顔色を改め、足取りを慎み、言葉は足りないかのようであった。裾をつまんで堂に上るときは身をかがめ、息を潜めて息をしていないかのようであった。退出して一段下りると顔をほころばせ、和やかになった。階段を下りきると小走りに進み、翼を広げたようであった。自分の位置に戻ると、恭しくかしこまった。

10.5.en: Holding the jade tablet, he bowed as if it were too heavy to bear. He raised it as if bowing and lowered it as if handing something over. His face was grave as if in fear, and his steps were short as if following a line. At the presentation of gifts, his face was composed; at a private meeting, he was cheerful.
10.5.ja: 圭を執るときは身をかがめ、重さに堪えないかのようであった。上げるときは会釈するように、下げるときは物を授けるようにした。顔色は改まって恐れるようで、足は小刻みに、線をたどるようであった。献上の儀では和やかな顔色、私的な会見では打ち解けていた。

10.6.en: The gentleman did not use dark purple or puce for trimmings, nor red or purple for everyday clothes. In hot weather he wore unlined fine or coarse linen, always over an inner garment. With a black robe, lambskin; with a white robe, fawnskin; with a yellow robe, fox fur. His everyday fur coat was long, with the right sleeve short. He always had a sleeping garment one and a half times his body length. Thick fox and badger furs were for sitting at home. Out of mourning, he wore all his pendants. Except for the ceremonial skirt, his skirts were cut narrower. He did not wear lambskin and a black cap to offer condolences. On the first day of the month, he always went to court in court dress.
10.6.ja: 君子は紺や緅で縁取りをせず、紅や紫を普段着にしなかった。暑いときは単衣の葛布を着たが、必ず上に羽織って出た。黒い衣には子羊の皮衣、白い衣には子鹿の皮衣、黄色の衣には狐の皮衣。普段の皮衣は長く、右の袖を短くした。必ず寝間着があり、長さは身長の一倍半。狐や貉の厚い毛皮は家での座に用いた。喪が明ければ、何でも佩びた。礼服の裳でなければ、必ず裁って縫った。子羊の皮衣と黒い冠では弔問しなかった。月の初めには、必ず朝服で朝廷に出た。

10.7.en: When fasting, he always had a clean garment of plain cloth. When fasting, he always changed his diet and moved to a different place to sit.
10.7.ja: 斎戒するときは、必ず清潔な布の衣を用いた。斎戒するときは、必ず食事を改め、居所を移した。

10.8.en: He did not tire of finely polished rice or of finely sliced meat. Rice that had spoiled and turned sour, fish gone bad, or meat that had rotted, he did not eat. Food of bad color he did not eat; food of bad smell he did not eat. Food badly cooked he did not eat; food out of season he did not eat. Meat not cut properly he did not eat; without the right sauce he did not eat. Even when there was much meat, he did not let it overpower the rice. Only in wine he set no limit, but never to the point of disorder. Wine and dried meat bought at the market he did not eat. He did not do without ginger, but did not eat much. After a sacrifice at the duke's, he did not keep the meat overnight. Sacrificial meat he did not keep beyond three days; beyond three days, he would not eat it. He did not converse while eating, nor talk in bed. Even with coarse rice and vegetable soup, he offered some in sacrifice, always with reverence.
10.8.ja: 飯は精白を厭わず、膾は細かいのを厭わなかった。飯が饐えて味が変わり、魚が腐り肉が傷んだものは食べなかった。色の悪いもの、臭いの悪いものは食べなかった。煮え方の悪いもの、時季外れのものは食べなかった。切り方の正しくないもの、合う醤のないものは食べなかった。肉が多くても飯より多くは食べなかった。酒だけは量を決めなかったが、乱れるまでは飲まなかった。市で買った酒や干し肉は食べなかった。生姜は欠かさなかったが、多くは食べなかった。君公の祭りの肉は翌日に持ち越さず、家の祭肉は三日を越えず、三日を越えたら食べなかった。食べるときは語らず、寝るときは話さなかった。粗末な飯や菜の汁でも、必ず少し供えて、恭しくした。

10.9.en: If the mat was not straight, he did not sit.
10.9.ja: 席が正しくなければ座らなかった。

10.10.en: When villagers drank together, he left only after those with walking staffs had left. When villagers held the exorcism, he stood on the eastern steps in court dress.
10.10.ja: 村人の酒宴では、杖をつく老人が退出してから退出した。村人が儺の祭りをするときは、朝服を着て東の階段に立った。

10.11.en: When sending a messenger to inquire after someone in another state, he bowed twice as he sent him off. When Ji Kangzi sent him medicine, he bowed and accepted it, saying: I do not know this medicine, so I dare not taste it.
10.11.ja: 他国の人に使いを送って安否を問うときは、二度拝して送り出した。康子が薬を贈ると、拝して受け、「私はこれをよく知らないので、あえて口にしません」と言った。

10.12.en: The stables burned down. Returning from court, the Master said: Was anyone hurt? He did not ask about the horses.
10.12.ja: 馬屋が焼けた。先生は朝廷から退いて言われた。「人に怪我はなかったか。」馬のことは問われなかった。

10.13.en: When the ruler gave him cooked food, he would straighten his mat and taste it first. When the ruler gave him raw meat, he would cook it and offer it to his ancestors. When the ruler gave him a live animal, he would raise it. When dining in attendance on the ruler, while the ruler made the offering, he would taste the food first. When he was ill and the ruler came to see him, he lay with his head to the east, with his court robe laid over him and his sash drawn across. When summoned by the ruler's command, he set off without waiting for his carriage to be yoked. Entering the Grand Temple, he asked about everything.
10.13.ja: 君主から食べ物を賜れば、必ず席を正して先に味わった。生肉を賜れば、必ず煮て祖先に供えた。生きた動物を賜れば、必ず飼った。君主に陪食するときは、君主が祭る間に先に食べた。病気で君主が見舞いに来られると、頭を東に向け、朝服をかけ、大帯を引き渡した。君主のお召しがあれば、馬車の支度を待たずに出かけた。大廟に入ると、一つ一つ尋ねた。

10.14.en: When a friend died with no one to take charge, he said: Let the funeral be held at my house. For gifts from friends, even a carriage and horses, he did not bow unless it was sacrificial meat.
10.14.ja: 友人が死んで身寄りがないと、「私の家で殯をしよう」と言った。友人からの贈り物は、車馬であっても、祭肉でなければ拝さなかった。

10.15.en: He did not sleep stretched out like a corpse, nor sit at home with formal bearing. When he saw someone in mourning dress, even an intimate, his expression changed. When he saw someone in ceremonial cap or a blind man, even someone he saw often, he showed proper bearing. To one in mourning clothes he bowed from his carriage; he bowed to those carrying the registers of the state. When a fine feast was served, his expression changed and he rose. At sudden thunder or violent wind, his expression changed.
10.15.ja: 寝るときは死体のように手足を伸ばさず、家にいるときは堅苦しくしなかった。喪服の人を見ると、親しい者でも必ず改まった。冠をつけた人や目の見えない人を見ると、なじみの者でも必ず礼をもって接した。喪服の人には車上で礼をし、戸籍の版を負う者にも礼をした。盛大なごちそうが出れば、必ず顔色を改めて立ち上がった。激しい雷や強い風には、必ず居ずまいを改めた。

10.16.en: Mounting his carriage, he always stood upright and held the strap. In the carriage, he did not look around, did not speak hurriedly, and did not point.
10.16.ja: 車に乗るときは、必ずまっすぐに立って綱を執った。車中では振り返らず、早口で話さず、指ささなかった。

10.17.en: Seeing the look on their faces, the birds rose, circled, and then settled together. He said: The hen pheasants on the mountain bridge — how timely! How timely! Zilu bowed to them; they sniffed three times and flew off.
10.17.ja: 顔色を見るとすぐ飛び立ち、空を巡ってから集まって止まる。先生が言われた。「山の橋の雌の雉、時を得ているな、時を得ているな。」子路がこれに向かって手を拱くと、三度においをかいで飛び立った。

11.1.en: The Master said: Those who first advanced in ritual and music were country folk; those who later advanced in ritual and music were gentlemen. If I were to use them, I would follow those who came first.
11.1.ja: 先生が言われた。先輩たちの礼楽は野人のようで、後輩たちの礼楽は君子のようだ。もし用いるなら、私は先輩たちに従う。

11.2.en: The Master said: Those who followed me in Chen and Cai are no longer at my gate. In virtuous conduct: Yan Yuan, Min Ziqian, Ran Boniu, Zhonggong. In speech: Zai Wo, Zigong. In government: Ran You, Jilu. In culture and learning: Ziyou, Zixia.
11.2.ja: 先生が言われた。陳・蔡で私に従った者は、みな今は門下にいない。徳行には顔淵・閔子騫・冉伯牛・仲弓。言語には宰我・子貢。政事には冉有・季路。文学には子游・子夏。

11.3.en: The Master said: Hui is no help to me; there is nothing I say that he is not pleased with.
11.3.ja: 先生が言われた。回は私を助けてくれる者ではない。私の言うことで喜ばないものがない。

11.4.en: The Master said: How filial Min Ziqian is! No one can find fault with what his parents and brothers say of him.
11.4.ja: 先生が言われた。孝行だな、閔子騫は。人々は彼の父母兄弟がほめる言葉に異を唱えない。

11.5.en: Nan Rong repeated the lines on the white jade tablet three times a day, and Confucius gave him his elder brother's daughter as wife.
11.5.ja: 南容が白圭の詩を何度も繰り返し唱えたので、孔子は兄の娘を彼に嫁がせた。

11.6.en: Ji Kangzi asked which of the disciples loved learning. Confucius replied: There was Yan Hui who loved learning. Unfortunately, his life was short and he died. Now there is no one.
11.6.ja: 季康子が「弟子の中で誰が学を好みますか」と問うた。孔子は答えられた。「顔回という者がいて学を好みましたが、不幸にも短命で死にました。今はもういません。」

11.7.en: When Yan Yuan died, Yan Lu asked for the Master's carriage to make an outer coffin for him. The Master said: Talented or not, each speaks of his own son. When Li died, he had an inner coffin but no outer coffin. I did not go on foot to make an outer coffin for him. Since I follow behind the ministers, I cannot go on foot.
11.7.ja: 顔淵が死ぬと、顔路は先生の車を売って外棺を作りたいと願った。先生「才があってもなくても、それぞれ自分の子のことを言う。鯉が死んだときも、内棺だけで外棺はなかった。私は歩いてまで彼のために外棺を作りはしなかった。私は大夫の末席に連なる者として、歩くわけにはいかないのだ。」

11.8.en: When Yan Yuan died, the Master said: Alas! Heaven has destroyed me! Heaven has destroyed me!
11.8.ja: 顔淵が死んだ。先生は言われた。「ああ、天は私を滅ぼした。天は私を滅ぼした。」

11.9.en: When Yan Yuan died, the Master wept for him with abandon. His followers said: Master, you weep with abandon. He said: Do I? If not for this man, for whom should I weep so?
11.9.ja: 顔淵が死に、先生は身もだえして泣かれた。従者が「先生は身もだえしておられます」と言うと、先生「そうか。この人のために嘆かなくて、誰のために嘆こう。」

11.10.en: When Yan Yuan died, the disciples wanted to give him a lavish burial. The Master said: No. The disciples gave him a lavish burial. The Master said: Hui looked on me as a father, yet I could not treat him as a son. It was not I; it was you, my friends.
11.10.ja: 顔淵が死に、門人が手厚く葬ろうとした。先生「いけない。」門人は手厚く葬った。先生「回は私を父のように見てくれたのに、私は彼を子のように扱えなかった。私のせいではない、諸君のせいだ。」

11.11.en: Jilu asked about serving the spirits. The Master said: You cannot yet serve people; how can you serve spirits? He ventured to ask about death. The Master said: You do not yet understand life; how can you understand death?
11.11.ja: 季路が鬼神に仕えることを問うた。先生「まだ人に仕えることもできないのに、どうして鬼に仕えられよう。」「あえて死について伺います。」「まだ生もわからないのに、どうして死がわかろう。」

11.12.en: Min Ziqian stood beside the Master, respectful and exact; Zilu, bold and firm; Ran You and Zigong, direct and at ease. The Master was pleased. 'As for You, I fear he will not die a natural death.'
11.12.ja: 閔子が傍らに控えると慎み深く正しく、子路は剛強で、冉有・子貢は和やかに率直であった。先生は楽しまれた。「由のような者は、まともな死に方はできないだろう。」

11.13.en: The people of Lu were rebuilding the Long Treasury. Min Ziqian said: Why not keep it as it was? Why must it be rebuilt? The Master said: That man seldom speaks, but when he speaks, he hits the mark.
11.13.ja: 魯の人が長府を建て直した。閔子騫が言った。「元のままでどうか。何も改めて作る必要はない。」先生「あの人はめったに物を言わないが、言えば必ず的に当たる。」

11.14.en: The Master said: What is You's zither doing at my gate? The disciples stopped respecting Zilu. The Master said: You has ascended to the hall, though he has not yet entered the inner room.
11.14.ja: 先生が言われた。「由の瑟が、どうして私の門で鳴っているのか。」門人は子路を敬わなくなった。先生「由は堂には上っている。まだ室に入っていないだけだ。」

11.15.en: Zigong asked: Who is the worthier, Shi or Shang? The Master said: Shi goes too far; Shang does not go far enough. Then is Shi better? The Master said: Going too far is the same as not going far enough.
11.15.ja: 子貢が問うた。「師と商とでは、どちらが賢いでしょう。」先生「師は行き過ぎ、商は及ばない。」「では師がまさっているのですか。」「過ぎたるは猶及ばざるがごとし。」

11.16.en: The Ji family was richer than the Duke of Zhou, yet Qiu collected taxes for them and added to their wealth. The Master said: He is no disciple of mine. You may beat the drum and attack him, my young friends.
11.16.ja: 季氏は周公より富んでいたのに、求は彼のために税を取り立てて、さらに富を増やした。先生「わが徒ではない。諸君、太鼓を鳴らして彼を責めてよい。」

11.17.en: Chai is simple, Shen is slow, Shi is showy, You is coarse.
11.17.ja: 柴は愚直、参は鈍重、師は見栄っ張り、由は粗野である。

11.18.en: The Master said: Hui comes close, yet he is often in want. Ci does not accept his lot and goes into trade; his guesses often hit the mark.
11.18.ja: 先生が言われた。回は道に近いが、しばしば窮乏している。賜は天命を受け入れずに商売をし、予想はよく当たる。

11.19.en: Zizhang asked about the way of the good man. The Master said: He does not follow in others' footsteps, yet he does not enter the inner room.
11.19.ja: 子張が善人の道を問うた。先生「先人の足跡を踏まないが、まだ室には入らない。」

11.20.en: The Master said: Approving of someone because his talk is earnest — is he a true gentleman, or only grave in appearance?
11.20.ja: 先生が言われた。言論が篤実だからといって認めるなら、それは君子だろうか、それとも顔つきだけ荘重な者だろうか。

11.21.en: Zilu asked: Should I act at once on what I hear? The Master said: While your father and elder brothers are alive, how can you act at once on what you hear? Ran You asked: Should I act at once on what I hear? The Master said: Act at once on what you hear. Gongxi Hua said: When You asked, you said 'your father and elder brothers are alive'; when Qiu asked, you said 'act at once.' I am confused and venture to ask. The Master said: Qiu holds back, so I urged him on; You has the drive of two men, so I held him back.
11.21.ja: 子路が「聞いたらすぐ行うべきですか」と問うた。先生「父兄がおられるのに、どうして聞いてすぐ行えよう。」冉有が同じことを問うた。先生「聞いたらすぐ行え。」公西華が言った。「由の問いには父兄がおられると言い、求の問いにはすぐ行えと言われました。赤は迷います、あえて伺います。」先生「求は引っ込み思案だから進めた。由は人を凌ぐから退けたのだ。」

11.22.en: The Master was in peril in Kuang, and Yan Yuan fell behind. The Master said: I thought you were dead. He said: While you live, Master, how would I dare die?
11.22.ja: 先生が匡で危難にあわれたとき、顔淵が遅れてやって来た。先生「お前は死んだと思ったぞ。」顔淵「先生がおられるのに、回がどうして死ねましょう。」

11.23.en: Ji Ziran asked: Can Zhong You and Ran Qiu be called great ministers? The Master said: I thought you would ask about someone remarkable, but you ask about You and Qiu. What is called a great minister serves his ruler by the Way, and when he cannot, he resigns. Now You and Qiu may be called ministers to fill a post. Then would they just go along? The Master said: In killing a father or a ruler, they would not go along.
11.23.ja: 季子然が問うた。「仲由・冉求は大臣と言えますか。」先生「もっと変わった問いかと思えば、由と求のことか。いわゆる大臣とは、道をもって君に仕え、できなければ辞める者だ。今の由と求は、数をそろえる臣と言えよう。」「では言いなりになるのですか。」「父や君を殺すことには従わない。」

11.24.en: Zilu had Zigao made steward of Bi. The Master said: You are harming another man's son. Zilu said: There are people there, and altars to the land and grain. Why must one read books before one counts as learned? The Master said: This is why I dislike glib talkers.
11.24.ja: 子路が子羔を費の宰にした。先生「人の子を損なうことになる。」子路「民がいて社稷があります。どうして書物を読んでから学んだとする必要がありましょう。」先生「だから口先のうまい者は嫌いなのだ。」

11.25.en: Zilu, Zeng Xi, Ran You, and Gongxi Hua sat in attendance. The Master said: Because I am a little older than you, do not hold back on my account. You often say, 'No one knows me.' If someone did know you, what would you do? Zilu answered at once: A state of a thousand chariots, hemmed in between great states, beset by armies and then by famine — if I governed it, in three years I could give the people courage and a sense of direction. The Master smiled at him. Qiu, what about you? He answered: A territory of sixty or seventy li, or fifty or sixty — if I governed it, in three years I could make the people have enough. As for ritual and music, I would wait for a gentleman. Chi, what about you? He answered: I do not say I could do it, but I would like to learn. At the ancestral temple, or at assemblies of the lords, in robe and cap, I would like to be a junior assistant. Dian, what about you? His zither-playing slowed, it rang out, and he set it aside and rose. He answered: Mine is different from what these three have chosen. The Master said: What harm is there? Each is just speaking of his aims. He said: In late spring, when the spring clothes are made, with five or six young men and six or seven boys, to bathe in the Yi, enjoy the breeze at the rain altar, and come home singing. The Master sighed deeply and said: I am with Dian! When the three went out, Zeng Xi stayed behind and said: What did you think of what those three said? The Master said: Each was just speaking of his aims. Why did you smile at You? To govern a state takes ritual, and his words were not modest; that is why I smiled. And was Qiu not speaking of a state? How is a territory of sixty or seventy li not a state? And was Chi not speaking of a state? The ancestral temple and assemblies — what are they if not the business of the lords? If Chi would be a junior, who could be a senior?
11.25.ja: 子路・曾皙・冉有・公西華が先生のそばに座っていた。先生「私が少し年長だからといって遠慮するな。普段『誰も自分をわかってくれない』と言っているが、もしわかってくれる人がいたら、どうするか。」子路がすぐに答えた。「千乗の国が大国の間に挟まれ、軍に攻められ、飢饉が重なる。由が治めれば三年で、民に勇気を持たせ、道を知らせましょう。」先生は微笑まれた。「求、お前はどうだ。」「六、七十里か五、六十里の国を求が治めれば、三年で民を満ち足りさせましょう。礼楽は君子を待ちます。」「赤、お前はどうだ。」「できるとは言いませんが、学びたいと思います。宗廟の祭りや諸侯の会同で、礼服と冠をつけて、小さな補佐役を務めたいと思います。」「点、お前はどうだ。」瑟の音がまばらになり、かたりと置いて立ち上がった。「三人の方とは違います。」先生「何の差し支えがあろう。それぞれ志を言うだけだ。」「晩春に春の服ができあがり、若者五、六人、子ども六、七人と沂水で浴し、舞雩で風に吹かれ、歌いながら帰りたいと思います。」先生はため息をついて言われた。「私は点に賛成だ。」三人が出て、曾皙が残った。曾皙「三人の話はいかがでしたか。」先生「それぞれ志を言っただけだ。」「先生はなぜ由に微笑まれたのですか。」「国を治めるには礼が要るのに、言葉に謙譲がなかった。だから微笑んだのだ。求の話は国のことではないのか。六、七十里や五、六十里が国でないことがあろうか。赤の話も国のことではないのか。宗廟や会同が諸侯のことでなくて何であろう。赤が小さな役なら、誰が大きな役を務められよう。」

12.1.en: Yan Yuan asked about humaneness. The Master said: To overcome the self and return to ritual is humaneness. If for one day one could overcome the self and return to ritual, the whole realm would turn to humaneness. Practicing humaneness comes from oneself — how could it come from others? Yan Yuan said: May I ask for the details? The Master said: Look at nothing contrary to ritual; listen to nothing contrary to ritual; say nothing contrary to ritual; do nothing contrary to ritual. Yan Yuan said: Though I am not quick, I will make these words my task.
12.1.ja: 顔淵が仁を問うた。先生「己に克って礼に復るのが仁である。一日でも己に克って礼に復れば、天下は仁に帰する。仁を行うのは自分による。人によるものだろうか。」顔淵「その細目をお聞かせください。」先生「礼でなければ視るな、礼でなければ聴くな、礼でなければ言うな、礼でなければ動くな。」顔淵「回は鈍いですが、この言葉に努めさせていただきます。」

12.2.en: Zhonggong asked about humaneness. The Master said: Going out the gate, act as if receiving an honored guest; employing the people, act as if conducting a great sacrifice. What you do not want for yourself, do not do to others. In the state, there will be no resentment; in the family, there will be no resentment. Zhonggong said: Though I am not quick, I will make these words my task.
12.2.ja: 仲弓が仁を問うた。先生「門を出れば大切な客に会うようにし、民を使うには大祭を執り行うようにする。己の欲せざる所は人に施すことなかれ。国にいても恨みがなく、家にいても恨みがない。」仲弓「雍は鈍いですが、この言葉に努めさせていただきます。」

12.3.en: Sima Niu asked about humaneness. The Master said: The humane are slow to speak. He said: Slow to speak — is that all it takes to be called humane? The Master said: When doing is hard, can one help being slow to speak?
12.3.ja: 司馬牛が仁を問うた。先生「仁者はその言葉が控えめだ。」「言葉が控えめなら、それで仁と言えるのですか。」先生「行うのが難しいのだから、言うのに控えめにならずにいられようか。」

12.4.en: Sima Niu asked about the gentleman. The Master said: The gentleman neither worries nor fears. He said: Neither worrying nor fearing — is that all it takes to be called a gentleman? The Master said: If one looks within and finds nothing amiss, what is there to worry about or fear?
12.4.ja: 司馬牛が君子を問うた。先生「君子は憂えず懼れない。」「憂えず懼れなければ、それで君子と言えるのですか。」先生「内に省みてやましくなければ、何を憂え何を懼れよう。」

12.5.en: Sima Niu said sorrowfully: Everyone has brothers; I alone have none. Zixia said: I have heard this: life and death are a matter of fate; wealth and rank rest with Heaven. If a gentleman is reverent and makes no mistakes, respectful to others and observant of ritual, then all within the four seas are his brothers. Why should a gentleman worry about having no brothers?
12.5.ja: 司馬牛が憂えて言った。「人にはみな兄弟があるのに、私だけない。」子夏「商はこう聞いている。死生命あり、富貴天にあり。君子が慎んで過ちなく、人に恭しく礼があれば、四海の内はみな兄弟である。君子がどうして兄弟のないことを憂えよう。」

12.6.en: Zizhang asked about clear-sightedness. The Master said: One on whom slander that seeps in slowly and complaints that cut to the skin have no effect may be called clear-sighted. One on whom they have no effect may be called far-sighted.
12.6.ja: 子張が明を問うた。先生「じわじわしみこむ讒言や、肌に迫る訴えが通じない者は、明と言える。それらが通じない者は、遠と言える。」

12.7.en: Zigong asked about government. The Master said: Enough food, enough arms, and the trust of the people. Zigong said: If one had no choice but to give up one of the three, which first? The Master said: Give up arms. Zigong said: If one had no choice but to give up one of the remaining two, which first? The Master said: Give up food. Since ancient times, all have died; without the people's trust, nothing stands.
12.7.ja: 子貢が政を問うた。先生「食を足らし、兵を足らし、民に信頼させる。」子貢「やむを得ず一つ捨てるなら、三つのうちどれを先にしますか。」「兵を捨てる。」「やむを得ず残り二つから捨てるなら。」「食を捨てる。昔から人はみな死ぬ。民に信がなければ立たない。」

12.8.en: Ji Zicheng said: A gentleman is substance, that is all; what need is there for refinement? Zigong said: What a pity, sir, that you speak of the gentleman so! A team of four horses cannot overtake the tongue. Refinement is as important as substance, and substance as refinement. The hide of a tiger or leopard, stripped of its hair, is just like the hide of a dog or sheep.
12.8.ja: 棘子成が言った。「君子は質だけでよい。文など何になろう。」子貢「惜しいことだ、あなたの君子論は。四頭立ての馬車も舌には追いつかない。文は質のごとく、質は文のごとし。虎や豹のなめし革も、毛を除けば犬や羊のなめし革と同じだ。」

12.9.en: Duke Ai asked You Ruo: The harvest is poor and there is not enough for expenses. What should be done? You Ruo replied: Why not tax at one tenth? The Duke said: Even at two tenths I do not have enough; how could I tax at one tenth? He replied: When the people have enough, how can the ruler not have enough? When the people do not have enough, how can the ruler have enough?
12.9.ja: 哀公が有若に問うた。「凶作で費用が足りない。どうしよう。」有若「十分の一の税にしてはいかがですか。」公「十分の二でも足りないのに、どうして十分の一にできよう。」有若「民が足りれば、君は誰と不足しましょう。民が足りなければ、君は誰と足りましょう。」

12.10.en: Zizhang asked about exalting virtue and discerning delusion. The Master said: Hold loyalty and good faith as primary and move toward what is right — that is exalting virtue. When you love someone you want him to live; when you hate him you want him to die. Wanting him to live and also wanting him to die — that is delusion. 'Truly it is not for wealth, but only for something different.'
12.10.ja: 子張が徳を崇くし惑いを弁えることを問うた。先生「忠信を主とし、義に移る。これが徳を崇くすることだ。愛すればその生を願い、憎めばその死を願う。生を願いながら死も願う。これが惑いだ。『まことに富のためでなく、ただ異なるもののため』。」

12.11.en: Duke Jing of Qi asked Confucius about government. Confucius replied: Let the ruler be a ruler, the minister a minister, the father a father, the son a son. The Duke said: Excellent! Truly, if the ruler is not a ruler, the minister not a minister, the father not a father, the son not a son, even if there is grain, would I get to eat it?
12.11.ja: 斉の景公が孔子に政を問うた。孔子「君は君らしく、臣は臣らしく、父は父らしく、子は子らしく。」公「よいことだ。まことに君が君らしくなく、臣が臣らしくなく、父が父らしくなく、子が子らしくなければ、穀物があっても、私は食べられようか。」

12.12.en: The Master said: One who could settle a lawsuit with half a word — that would be You, would it not? Zilu never slept on a promise.
12.12.ja: 先生が言われた。一言で訴訟を裁けるのは、由であろうか。子路は約束を翌日に持ち越さなかった。

12.13.en: The Master said: In hearing lawsuits I am like anyone else. What is needed is to make sure there are no lawsuits!
12.13.ja: 先生が言われた。訴えを聴くことなら、私も人並みだ。大事なのは訴えをなくすことだ。

12.14.en: Zizhang asked about government. The Master said: Hold your post without weariness, and carry it out with loyalty.
12.14.ja: 子張が政を問うた。先生「位にあって倦まず、行うには忠をもってする。」

12.15.en: The Master said: Learn broadly in culture and restrain it with ritual, and you may thereby avoid going astray.
12.15.ja: 先生が言われた。広く文を学び、礼でそれを締めくくれば、道に背かずにいられるだろう。

12.16.en: The Master said: The gentleman helps others achieve what is good in them, not what is bad. The petty man does the opposite.
12.16.ja: 先生が言われた。君子は人の美点を成し遂げさせ、悪いところは成し遂げさせない。小人はその反対だ。

12.17.en: Ji Kangzi asked Confucius about government. Confucius replied: To govern is to be correct. If you lead by being correct, who will dare not be correct?
12.17.ja: 季康子が孔子に政を問うた。孔子「政とは正である。あなたが正しく率いれば、誰が正しくないことをしようか。」

12.18.en: Ji Kangzi was troubled by thieves and asked Confucius. Confucius replied: If you yourself did not covet, they would not steal even if you rewarded them for it.
12.18.ja: 季康子が盗人に悩んで孔子に問うた。孔子「もしあなたが欲を持たなければ、褒美を与えても盗みはしないでしょう。」

12.19.en: Ji Kangzi asked Confucius about government: What if I killed those without the Way in order to bring about the Way? Confucius replied: In governing, why use killing? If you desire the good, the people will be good. The virtue of the gentleman is the wind; the virtue of the petty man is the grass. When the wind passes over the grass, it surely bends.
12.19.ja: 季康子が孔子に政を問うた。「道に外れた者を殺して、道ある者に就かせたらどうでしょう。」孔子「政をなすのに、どうして殺す必要がありましょう。あなたが善を望めば、民は善くなります。君子の徳は風、小人の徳は草。草に風が吹けば、必ずなびきます。」

12.20.en: Zizhang asked: What must a scholar be like to be called accomplished? The Master said: What do you mean by accomplished? Zizhang replied: Known throughout the state, known throughout the clan. The Master said: That is being known, not being accomplished. The accomplished man is upright in substance and loves what is right; he weighs people's words and observes their looks, and is mindful to put himself below others. He is sure to succeed in the state and in the clan. As for the man who is merely known, he puts on a look of humaneness but acts against it, and dwells in this without doubt. He is sure to be known in the state and in the clan.
12.20.ja: 子張が問うた。「士はどうであれば達と言えますか。」先生「お前の言う達とは何か。」子張「国にいても必ず評判になり、家にいても必ず評判になることです。」先生「それは聞であって達ではない。達とは、質朴でまっすぐで義を好み、言葉を察し顔色を見て、人にへりくだることを心がける。国にいても家にいても必ず通る。聞とは、顔つきは仁を装いながら行いは背き、それに安住して疑わない。国にいても家にいても必ず評判にはなる。」

12.21.en: Fan Chi was walking with the Master below the rain altar and said: May I ask about exalting virtue, rooting out hidden faults, and discerning delusion? The Master said: A good question! Putting the work first and the reward after — is that not exalting virtue? Attacking your own faults and not those of others — is that not rooting out hidden faults? In a morning's anger forgetting yourself and even your parents — is that not delusion?
12.21.ja: 樊遅が先生のお供をして舞雩の下を歩いたとき言った。「あえて徳を崇くし、隠れた悪を修め、惑いを弁えることを伺います。」先生「よい問いだ。事を先にして得ることを後にする、徳を崇くすることではないか。自分の悪を攻めて人の悪を攻めない、隠れた悪を修めることではないか。一時の怒りで身を忘れ、親にまで及ぼす、惑いではないか。」

12.22.en: Fan Chi asked about humaneness. The Master said: Love others. He asked about wisdom. The Master said: Know others. Fan Chi did not understand. The Master said: Raise up the straight and set them over the crooked, and the crooked can be made straight. Fan Chi withdrew and went to see Zixia, saying: Just now I saw the Master and asked about wisdom, and he said, 'Raise up the straight and set them over the crooked, and the crooked can be made straight.' What does this mean? Zixia said: How rich these words are! When Shun held the realm, he chose from among the many and raised up Gao Yao, and the inhumane went far away. When Tang held the realm, he chose from among the many and raised up Yi Yin, and the inhumane went far away.
12.22.ja: 樊遅が仁を問うた。先生「人を愛することだ。」知を問うた。「人を知ることだ。」樊遅にはわからなかった。先生「まっすぐな者を挙げて曲がった者の上に置けば、曲がった者をまっすぐにできる。」樊遅は退いて子夏に会って言った。「さきほど先生に知を問うたら、まっすぐな者を挙げて曲がった者の上に置けば曲がった者をまっすぐにできる、と言われた。どういう意味か。」子夏「豊かな言葉だ。舜が天下を治めたとき、衆人から選んで皐陶を挙げると、不仁の者は遠ざかった。湯が天下を治めたとき、衆人から選んで伊尹を挙げると、不仁の者は遠ざかった。」

12.23.en: Zigong asked about friendship. The Master said: Advise him faithfully and guide him well; if that fails, stop. Do not bring humiliation on yourself.
12.23.ja: 子貢が友を問うた。先生「誠意をもって忠告し、よく導く。聞かれなければやめる。自ら辱めを受けてはならない。」

12.24.en: Zengzi said: The gentleman gathers friends through culture, and through friends supports his humaneness.
12.24.ja: 曾子が言った。君子は文によって友と会し、友によって仁を助ける。

13.1.en: Zilu asked about government. The Master said: Go before the people and work hard for them. He asked for more. The Master said: Do not grow weary.
13.1.ja: 子路が政を問うた。先生「民に先立って行い、民のために骨を折る。」さらに尋ねると、「倦むことなかれ。」

13.2.en: Zhonggong, as steward of the Ji family, asked about government. The Master said: Put your officers first, pardon small faults, and raise up the worthy and talented. He said: How can I know the worthy and talented to raise them? The Master said: Raise those you know. Those you do not know — will others pass them over?
13.2.ja: 仲弓が季氏の宰となって政を問うた。先生「まず役人を先に立て、小さな過ちを許し、賢才を挙げよ。」「どうやって賢才を見分けて挙げるのですか。」「お前の知っている者を挙げよ。お前の知らない者を、人が捨てておくだろうか。」

13.3.en: Zilu said: The ruler of Wei is waiting for you to govern. What will you do first? The Master said: It must be to rectify names! Zilu said: Is that so? How impractical you are, Master! Why rectify them? The Master said: How crude you are, You! A gentleman leaves aside what he does not know. If names are not correct, speech does not follow; if speech does not follow, affairs do not succeed; if affairs do not succeed, ritual and music do not flourish; if ritual and music do not flourish, punishments miss the mark; if punishments miss the mark, the people do not know where to put hand or foot. So when a gentleman names something, it must be sayable; when he says it, it must be doable. In his words the gentleman allows nothing careless.
13.3.ja: 子路が言った。「衛の君が先生を待って政をさせようとしています。先生は何を先にしますか。」先生「必ず名を正すことだ。」子路「そんなことですか、先生は迂遠ですね。何を正すのですか。」先生「粗野だな、由は。君子は知らないことには口をつぐむものだ。名が正しくなければ言葉が順当でなく、言葉が順当でなければ事が成らず、事が成らなければ礼楽が興らず、礼楽が興らなければ刑罰が的を外れ、刑罰が的を外れれば民は手足の置き所がない。だから君子は名づければ必ず言えるようにし、言えば必ず行えるようにする。君子は言葉について、いいかげんにするところがないだけだ。」

13.4.en: Fan Chi asked to learn farming. The Master said: I am not as good as an old farmer. He asked to learn gardening. The Master said: I am not as good as an old gardener. Fan Chi went out. The Master said: What a petty man Fan Xu is! If those above love ritual, the people will not dare be irreverent; if those above love what is right, the people will not dare disobey; if those above love good faith, the people will not dare be insincere. If it is so, the people of the four quarters will come with their children strapped on their backs. What need is there for farming?
13.4.ja: 樊遅が稼穡を学びたいと願った。先生「私は老農に及ばない。」野菜作りを学びたいと願った。「私は老いた園丁に及ばない。」樊遅が出ていった。先生「小人だな、樊須は。上が礼を好めば民は敬わずにいられず、上が義を好めば民は従わずにいられず、上が信を好めば民は真心を尽くさずにいられない。そうなれば四方の民が子を背負ってやって来る。どうして稼穡など必要だろう。」

13.5.en: The Master said: One may recite the three hundred Odes, yet when given a post in government, fail to carry it out, and when sent on missions abroad, be unable to answer on his own. However many he has learned, what use are they?
13.5.ja: 先生が言われた。詩三百篇を暗誦しても、政を任せて果たせず、四方に使いして独りで応対できなければ、多く覚えていても何になろう。

13.6.en: The Master said: If he himself is correct, things are done without orders; if he himself is not correct, even with orders they are not obeyed.
13.6.ja: 先生が言われた。その身が正しければ、命じなくても行われる。その身が正しくなければ、命じても従わない。

13.7.en: The Master said: The governments of Lu and Wei are brothers.
13.7.ja: 先生が言われた。魯と衛の政は兄弟のようなものだ。

13.8.en: The Master said of Prince Jing of Wei that he managed his household well. When he first had something, he said: It will more or less do. When he had a little more, he said: It is more or less complete. When he was rich, he said: It is more or less fine.
13.8.ja: 先生が衛の公子荊について言われた。家をうまく保った。初めて少し持つと「まあ足りた」と言い、少し増えると「まあ整った」と言い、豊かになると「まあ立派だ」と言った。

13.9.en: The Master went to Wei, with Ran You driving. The Master said: How numerous the people are! Ran You said: Now that they are numerous, what more should be done? Make them prosperous. Now that they are prosperous, what more should be done? Teach them.
13.9.ja: 先生が衛に行かれ、冉有が御者をした。先生「人が多いな。」冉有「多くなったら、さらに何をしますか。」「富ませる。」「富んだら、さらに何をしますか。」「教える。」

13.10.en: The Master said: If anyone would employ me, within a year things would be in fair shape, and in three years there would be results.
13.10.ja: 先生が言われた。もし私を用いる者があれば、一年でまずまずになり、三年で成果をあげよう。

13.11.en: The Master said: 'If good men governed a state for a hundred years, they could overcome cruelty and do away with killing.' How true this saying is!
13.11.ja: 先生が言われた。「善人が国を治めて百年になれば、残虐に打ち勝ち殺戮をなくせる。」まことにこの言葉の通りだ。

13.12.en: The Master said: Even with a true king, it would take a generation for humaneness to prevail.
13.12.ja: 先生が言われた。王者が現れても、必ず一世代たってから仁が行きわたる。

13.13.en: The Master said: If he can make himself correct, what difficulty would he have in government? If he cannot make himself correct, how can he correct others?
13.13.ja: 先生が言われた。その身を正せば、政に従うのに何の難しいことがあろう。その身を正せなければ、どうして人を正せよう。

13.14.en: Ran Zi returned from court. The Master said: Why so late? He replied: There was state business. The Master said: It must have been family business. If there had been state business, though I am not in office, I would have heard of it.
13.14.ja: 冉子が朝廷から退出した。先生「なぜ遅かったのか。」「政務がありました。」先生「それは家の事務だろう。政務があれば、私は用いられていなくても、聞き及んでいるはずだ。」

13.15.en: Duke Ding asked: Is there a single saying that can make a state flourish? Confucius replied: A saying cannot be expected to do that much. But people say, 'It is hard to be a ruler, and not easy to be a minister.' If one understood how hard it is to be a ruler, would that not come close to a single saying making a state flourish? He asked: Is there a single saying that can ruin a state? Confucius replied: A saying cannot be expected to do that much. But people say, 'I take no joy in being ruler, except that no one contradicts what I say.' If what he says is good and no one contradicts it, is that not good? If what he says is not good and no one contradicts it, would that not come close to a single saying ruining a state?
13.15.ja: 定公が問うた。「一言で国を興せるということがあるか。」孔子「言葉にそこまで期待はできません。ただ人は『君たるは難く、臣たるも易からず』と言います。君たるの難しさを知れば、一言で国を興すに近くないでしょうか。」「一言で国を滅ぼすということがあるか。」孔子「言葉にそこまで期待はできません。ただ人は『君であることに楽しみはない、ただ私の言うことに誰も逆らわないだけだ』と言います。言うことが善くて誰も逆らわないなら、善いことではありませんか。善くないのに誰も逆らわないなら、一言で国を滅ぼすに近くないでしょうか。」

13.16.en: The Duke of She asked about government. The Master said: When those near are pleased and those far away come.
13.16.ja: 葉公が政を問うた。先生「近くの者は喜び、遠くの者はやって来る。」

13.17.en: Zixia, as steward of Jufu, asked about government. The Master said: Do not seek speed; do not look to small gains. Seek speed and you will not get there; look to small gains and great affairs will not be accomplished.
13.17.ja: 子夏が莒父の宰となって政を問うた。先生「速さを求めるな、小さな利を見るな。速さを求めれば達せず、小さな利を見れば大事は成らない。」

13.18.en: The Duke of She said to Confucius: In my village there is an upright man. When his father stole a sheep, the son bore witness against him. Confucius said: The upright in my village are different. The father covers for the son, and the son covers for the father. Uprightness lies in this.
13.18.ja: 葉公が孔子に言った。「私の村にまっすぐな躬という者がいる。父が羊を盗むと、子がそれを証言した。」孔子「私の村のまっすぐな者はそれとは違います。父は子のために隠し、子は父のために隠す。まっすぐさはその中にあります。」

13.19.en: Fan Chi asked about humaneness. The Master said: Be respectful at home, reverent in handling affairs, loyal in dealing with others. Even among the barbarian tribes, these cannot be abandoned.
13.19.ja: 樊遅が仁を問うた。先生「家にいるときは恭しく、事を執るときは敬み、人と交わるときは忠実に。夷狄の地へ行っても、これを捨ててはならない。」

13.20.en: Zigong asked: What must one be like to be called a scholar? The Master said: One who conducts himself with a sense of shame, and when sent abroad does not disgrace his ruler's commission, may be called a scholar. He said: May I ask about the next level? One whose clan praises his filial piety and whose village praises his respect for elders. May I ask about the next? One whose word is always kept and whose actions are always carried through — stubborn little men! Yet they may count as the next level. He said: What about those in government today? The Master said: Ah! Men of the peck and the bushel — hardly worth counting.
13.20.ja: 子貢が問うた。「どうであれば士と言えますか。」先生「自分の行いに恥を知り、四方に使いして君命を辱めなければ、士と言える。」「その次をあえて伺います。」「一族に孝行と称され、郷里に悌順と称される者。」「その次を伺います。」「言うことは必ず守り、行いは必ずやり遂げる。かたくなな小人だが、それでも次とは言える。」「今の政に携わる者はどうですか。」先生「ああ、升や籠ほどの器量の者たち、数えるに足りない。」

13.21.en: The Master said: If I cannot find those who walk the middle way to associate with, then I must have the ardent and the cautious! The ardent press forward; the cautious have things they will not do.
13.21.ja: 先生が言われた。中道を行く者と交われないなら、狂者か狷者だろう。狂者は進んで取り、狷者はしないことがある。

13.22.en: The Master said: The southerners have a saying: 'A man without constancy cannot even be a shaman or a doctor.' Well said! 'If one is not constant in his virtue, he may meet with disgrace.' The Master said: Such a man simply need not divine.
13.22.ja: 先生が言われた。南方の人の言葉に「人として恒心がなければ、巫医にもなれない」とある。よい言葉だ。「その徳が恒でなければ、恥を受けることがある。」先生が言われた。占うまでもないことだ。

13.23.en: The Master said: The gentleman is harmonious but does not conform; the petty man conforms but is not harmonious.
13.23.ja: 先生が言われた。君子は和して同ぜず、小人は同じて和せず。

13.24.en: Zigong asked: What if everyone in the village likes him? The Master said: Not enough. What if everyone in the village dislikes him? The Master said: Not enough. Better that the good people of the village like him and the bad ones dislike him.
13.24.ja: 子貢が問うた。「村人がみな好むなら、どうでしょう。」先生「まだよくない。」「村人がみな憎むなら、どうでしょう。」「まだよくない。村人の善い者が好み、善くない者が憎むのには及ばない。」

13.25.en: The Master said: The gentleman is easy to serve but hard to please. Try to please him by other than the Way, and he is not pleased; when he employs people, he uses each according to his capacity. The petty man is hard to serve but easy to please. Try to please him by other than the Way, and he is pleased; when he employs people, he expects everything of them.
13.25.ja: 先生が言われた。君子は仕えやすいが喜ばせにくい。道によらずに喜ばせようとしても喜ばない。人を使うときは器量に応じて使う。小人は仕えにくいが喜ばせやすい。道によらずに喜ばせても喜ぶ。人を使うときは何でもできることを求める。

13.26.en: The Master said: The gentleman is at ease but not arrogant; the petty man is arrogant but not at ease.
13.26.ja: 先生が言われた。君子は泰然として驕らず、小人は驕って泰然としない。

13.27.en: The Master said: Firm, resolute, simple, slow to speak — these are close to humaneness.
13.27.ja: 先生が言われた。剛毅木訥、仁に近し。

13.28.en: Zilu asked: What must one be like to be called a scholar? The Master said: Earnest, encouraging, and congenial — such a one may be called a scholar. Earnest and encouraging with friends, congenial with brothers.
13.28.ja: 子路が問うた。「どうであれば士と言えますか。」先生「切々として、偲々として、怡々としていれば、士と言える。友には切々偲々、兄弟には怡々と。」

13.29.en: The Master said: When a good man has taught the people for seven years, they too can be sent to war.
13.29.ja: 先生が言われた。善人が民を七年教えれば、戦に就かせることもできる。

13.30.en: The Master said: To send untrained people to war is to throw them away.
13.30.ja: 先生が言われた。教えていない民を戦わせるのは、民を捨てることだ。

14.1.en: Xian asked about shame. The Master said: When the state has the Way, to draw a salary; when the state lacks the Way, to draw a salary — that is shameful.
14.1.ja: 憲が恥を問うた。先生「国に道があっても禄を食み、国に道がなくても禄を食む。それが恥である。」

14.2.en: If one does not give way to domineering, boasting, resentment, or greed, can he be called humane? The Master said: He may be called hard to find; whether he is humane, I do not know.
14.2.ja: 「人に勝とうとすること、誇ること、恨むこと、欲張ることが行われなければ、仁と言えますか。」先生「難しいことだとは言えるが、仁かどうかは私にはわからない。」

14.3.en: The Master said: A scholar who cherishes his comfort is not worthy to be called a scholar.
14.3.ja: 先生が言われた。士でありながら住み心地を思うようでは、士とするに足りない。

14.4.en: The Master said: When the state has the Way, be lofty in speech and lofty in action; when the state lacks the Way, be lofty in action but modest in speech.
14.4.ja: 先生が言われた。国に道があれば、言葉を高く行いを高くする。国に道がなければ、行いは高くして言葉は控えめにする。

14.5.en: The Master said: Those with virtue are sure to have words worth hearing; those with words are not necessarily virtuous. The humane are sure to have courage; the courageous are not necessarily humane.
14.5.ja: 先生が言われた。徳のある者には必ずよい言葉があるが、言葉のある者に必ず徳があるとは限らない。仁者には必ず勇があるが、勇者に必ず仁があるとは限らない。

14.6.en: Nangong Kuo asked Confucius: Yi was a fine archer and Ao could push a boat over land, yet neither died a natural death. Yu and Ji labored at farming themselves, yet came to possess the realm. The Master did not answer. When Nangong Kuo had gone out, the Master said: What a gentleman that man is! How he esteems virtue!
14.6.ja: 南宮适が孔子に問うた。「羿は弓が巧みで、奡は陸で舟を押し動かしたが、どちらもまともな死に方をしなかった。禹と稷は自ら耕して天下を有した。」先生は答えられなかった。南宮适が出ていくと、先生「君子だな、この人は。徳を尊ぶな、この人は。」

14.7.en: The Master said: There may be gentlemen who are not humane, but there has never been a petty man who is humane.
14.7.ja: 先生が言われた。君子でも仁でない者はいるだろうが、小人で仁である者はいない。

14.8.en: The Master said: Can you love someone without making him work hard? Can you be loyal to someone without instructing him?
14.8.ja: 先生が言われた。愛するなら、苦労させずにいられようか。忠であるなら、教え諭さずにいられようか。

14.9.en: The Master said: In drafting state documents, Pi Chen made the first draft, Shishu examined and discussed it, the envoy Ziyu revised and polished it, and Zichan of Dongli gave it its final luster.
14.9.ja: 先生が言われた。外交文書を作るとき、裨諶が草稿を作り、世叔が検討し、行人の子羽が修正し、東里の子産が仕上げの潤色をした。

14.10.en: Someone asked about Zichan. The Master said: A kind man. He asked about Zixi. The Master said: That man! That man! He asked about Guan Zhong. The Master said: He was a man indeed. He took the three hundred households of Pian from the Bo family, and Bo, living on coarse food, never uttered a word of resentment to the end of his days.
14.10.ja: ある人が子産について問うた。先生「恵み深い人だ。」子西について問うと、「あの人か、あの人か。」管仲について問うと、「人物だ。伯氏の騈邑三百戸を取り上げたが、伯氏は粗末な飯を食べ、死ぬまで恨み言を言わなかった。」

14.11.en: The Master said: To be poor without resentment is hard; to be rich without arrogance is easy.
14.11.ja: 先生が言われた。貧しくて恨まないのは難しく、富んで驕らないのはやさしい。

14.12.en: The Master said: Meng Gongchuo would be more than fit to be chief retainer of the Zhao or Wei families, but he could not be a minister of Teng or Xue.
14.12.ja: 先生が言われた。孟公綽は趙・魏の家老なら余裕があるが、滕・薛の大夫にはなれない。

14.13.en: Zilu asked about the complete man. The Master said: One with the wisdom of Zang Wuzhong, the freedom from desire of Gongchuo, the courage of Bian Zhuangzi, and the skill of Ran Qiu, refined by ritual and music, may be called a complete man. He added: But why must the complete man of today be so? One who, seeing profit, thinks of what is right; seeing danger, offers his life; and does not forget a long-standing promise however long ago he made it — he too may be called a complete man.
14.13.ja: 子路が成人を問うた。先生「臧武仲の知、公綽の無欲、卞荘子の勇、冉求の芸があり、それを礼楽で飾れば、成人と言えよう。」さらに言われた。「今の成人は、そこまで必要だろうか。利を見ては義を思い、危うきを見ては命を授け、昔の約束をいつまでも忘れなければ、成人と言えよう。」

14.14.en: The Master asked Gongming Jia about Gongshu Wenzi: Is it true that your master does not speak, does not laugh, and does not take? Gongming Jia replied: Those who told you exaggerated. My master speaks only when it is time, so people do not tire of his speaking; he laughs only when he is happy, so people do not tire of his laughing; he takes only when it is right, so people do not tire of his taking. The Master said: Is that so? Can it really be so?
14.14.ja: 先生が公明賈に公叔文子のことを問うた。「本当ですか、あの方は言わず、笑わず、取らないというのは。」公明賈「伝えた者が言い過ぎです。あの方は時を得てから言うので、人はその言葉を嫌がりません。楽しくなってから笑うので、人はその笑いを嫌がりません。義にかなってから取るので、人はその取ることを嫌がりません。」先生「そうですか。本当にそうでしょうか。」

14.15.en: The Master said: Zang Wuzhong held on to Fang and demanded that an heir be appointed for him in Lu. Though he says he was not coercing his ruler, I do not believe it.
14.15.ja: 先生が言われた。臧武仲は防に拠って、魯に後継ぎを立てることを求めた。君主を脅したのではないと言っても、私は信じない。

14.16.en: The Master said: Duke Wen of Jin was crafty and not upright; Duke Huan of Qi was upright and not crafty.
14.16.ja: 先生が言われた。晋の文公は謀略を用いて正しくなく、斉の桓公は正しくて謀略を用いなかった。

14.17.en: Zilu said: Duke Huan had Prince Jiu killed. Shao Hu died with him, but Guan Zhong did not. Was he not lacking in humaneness? The Master said: Duke Huan gathered the lords together nine times without using war chariots — that was Guan Zhong's doing. Such was his humaneness! Such was his humaneness!
14.17.ja: 子路が言った。「桓公が公子糾を殺したとき、召忽は殉じたが、管仲は死ななかった。仁ではないのでは。」先生「桓公が諸侯を九たび会合させて、兵車を用いなかったのは、管仲の力だ。それこそ彼の仁だ、それこそ彼の仁だ。」

14.18.en: Zigong said: Was Guan Zhong not inhumane? When Duke Huan killed Prince Jiu, he could not die for him, and even became Huan's minister. The Master said: Guan Zhong served as Duke Huan's minister, made him leader of the lords, and set the whole realm in order; to this day the people enjoy his gifts. But for Guan Zhong, we would be wearing our hair loose and folding our robes to the left. Would he be like a common man or woman keeping petty faith, hanging himself in a ditch with no one knowing?
14.18.ja: 子貢が言った。「管仲は仁者ではないのでは。桓公が公子糾を殺したとき死ねず、しかも桓公の宰相となった。」先生「管仲は桓公を補佐して諸侯の覇者とし、天下を一つに正した。民は今もその恩恵を受けている。管仲がいなければ、私たちは髪をざんばらにし、衣を左前にしていただろう。どうして凡夫凡婦がつまらぬ義理立てをして、溝で首をくくり、誰にも知られないのと同じであろう。」

14.19.en: Zhuan, a household officer of Gongshu Wenzi, rose together with Wenzi to the ducal court. When the Master heard of it, he said: He deserves to be called Wen.
14.19.ja: 公叔文子の家臣の大夫僎は、文子とともに公朝に昇った。先生はこれを聞いて言われた。「文と諡されるにふさわしい。」

14.20.en: The Master spoke of Duke Ling of Wei's lack of the Way. Ji Kangzi said: If he is like that, why has he not lost his state? Confucius said: Zhongshu Yu handles foreign guests, Priest Tuo handles the ancestral temple, and Wangsun Jia handles the army. With such men, how would he lose it?
14.20.ja: 先生が衛の霊公の無道を語られた。康子「そうであるなら、どうして滅びないのですか。」孔子「仲叔圉が賓客を扱い、祝鮀が宗廟を治め、王孫賈が軍隊を治めています。そうであれば、どうして滅びましょう。」

14.21.en: The Master said: One who speaks without shame will find it hard to carry out his words.
14.21.ja: 先生が言われた。言うことに恥じらいがなければ、それを実行するのは難しい。

14.22.en: Chen Chengzi murdered Duke Jian. Confucius bathed and went to court, and reported to Duke Ai: Chen Heng has murdered his ruler. I request that he be punished. The Duke said: Tell the three lords. Confucius said: Because I follow behind the ministers, I dared not fail to report. And the ruler says, 'Tell the three lords.' He went to the three lords and told them; they refused. Confucius said: Because I follow behind the ministers, I dared not fail to report.
14.22.ja: 陳成子が簡公を弑した。孔子は沐浴して朝廷に出て、哀公に告げた。「陳恒がその君を弑しました。討伐をお願いします。」公「あの三人に告げよ。」孔子「私は大夫の末席にいる者として、告げないわけにはいかなかった。それなのに君は三人に告げよと言われる。」三人のところへ行って告げたが、聞き入れられなかった。孔子「私は大夫の末席にいる者として、告げないわけにはいかなかったのだ。」

14.23.en: Zilu asked about serving a ruler. The Master said: Do not deceive him, but stand up to him.
14.23.ja: 子路が君に仕えることを問うた。先生「欺いてはならない。そして諫めて逆らえ。」

14.24.en: The Master said: The gentleman reaches upward; the petty man reaches downward.
14.24.ja: 先生が言われた。君子は上に達し、小人は下に達する。

14.25.en: The Master said: In ancient times, people learned for their own sake; nowadays, people learn for the sake of others.
14.25.ja: 先生が言われた。昔の学ぶ者は自分のために学び、今の学ぶ者は人に見せるために学ぶ。

14.26.en: Qu Boyu sent a messenger to Confucius. Confucius sat with him and asked: What is your master doing? He replied: My master wishes to reduce his faults but has not yet managed it. When the messenger had left, the Master said: What a messenger! What a messenger!
14.26.ja: 蘧伯玉が孔子に使者を送った。孔子は使者と座って尋ねた。「あの方は何をしておられますか。」使者「あの方は過ちを少なくしようとしていますが、まだできていません。」使者が出ていくと、先生「立派な使者だ、立派な使者だ。」

14.27.en: The Master said: When not in the office, do not plan its affairs.
14.27.ja: 先生が言われた。その地位にいなければ、その政を謀らない。

14.28.en: Zengzi said: The gentleman does not let his thoughts go beyond his position.
14.28.ja: 曾子が言った。君子は思うことがその地位を出ない。

14.29.en: The Master said: The gentleman is ashamed to let his words outrun his deeds.
14.29.ja: 先生が言われた。君子は言葉が行いを上回ることを恥じる。

14.30.en: The Master said: The way of the gentleman has three parts, and I have achieved none of them: the humane do not worry, the wise are not perplexed, the brave do not fear. Zigong said: That is the Master describing himself.
14.30.ja: 先生が言われた。君子の道は三つあるが、私はどれもできない。仁者は憂えず、知者は惑わず、勇者は懼れない。子貢「それは先生がご自分のことを言われたのです。」

14.31.en: Zigong was comparing people. The Master said: Ci must be very worthy! As for me, I have no time for that.
14.31.ja: 子貢が人を比べて評していた。先生「賜は賢いのだな。私にはそんな暇はない。」

14.32.en: The Master said: Do not worry that others do not know you; worry that you lack ability.
14.32.ja: 先生が言われた。人が自分を知らないことを憂えず、自分にその能力がないことを憂える。

14.33.en: The Master said: Not anticipating deceit, not presuming bad faith, yet being the first to perceive it — that is worthy indeed!
14.33.ja: 先生が言われた。偽りを予期せず、不信を推測しない。それでいて先に気づく。これこそ賢いのだ。

14.34.en: Weisheng Mu said to Confucius: Qiu, why are you always so busily on the move? Are you not just a smooth talker? Confucius said: I would not dare be a smooth talker. It is stubbornness I dislike.
14.34.ja: 微生畝が孔子に言った。「丘よ、どうしてそうせわしなく動き回るのか。口先がうまいだけではないのか。」孔子「口先をうまくしようなどとは思いません。頑固なのが嫌なのです。」

14.35.en: The Master said: A fine steed is praised not for its strength but for its character.
14.35.ja: 先生が言われた。名馬はその力を称えられるのではなく、その徳を称えられるのだ。

14.36.en: Someone said: What about repaying injury with kindness? The Master said: Then with what would you repay kindness? Repay injury with uprightness, and repay kindness with kindness.
14.36.ja: ある人が言った。「徳をもって怨みに報いるのはどうですか。」先生「では何をもって徳に報いるのか。直をもって怨みに報い、徳をもって徳に報いる。」

14.37.en: The Master said: No one knows me! Zigong said: Why does no one know you? The Master said: I do not resent Heaven, nor blame others. I learn from below and reach up above. The one who knows me — is it Heaven?
14.37.ja: 先生が言われた。「私を知る者はいないな。」子貢「どうして先生を知る者がいないのですか。」先生「天を怨まず、人をとがめず、下学して上達する。私を知るのは天であろうか。」

14.38.en: Gongbo Liao slandered Zilu to Jisun. Zifu Jingbo reported it, saying: My master has certainly been misled by Gongbo Liao, but I still have the power to have his corpse displayed in the marketplace. The Master said: If the Way is to prevail, it is fate. If the Way is to be cast aside, it is fate. What can Gongbo Liao do against fate?
14.38.ja: 公伯寮が子路のことを季孫に讒言した。子服景伯がこれを告げて言った。「あの方は公伯寮に惑わされていますが、私の力でも彼を市にさらすことはできます。」先生「道が行われるのも命である。道が廃れるのも命である。公伯寮ごときが命をどうできよう。」

14.39.en: The Master said: The worthy withdraw from the world; the next withdraw from a place; the next withdraw at a look; the next withdraw at a word.
14.39.ja: 先生が言われた。賢者は世を避け、その次は地を避け、その次は顔色を見て避け、その次は言葉を聞いて避ける。

14.40.en: The Master said: Seven men have done so.
14.40.ja: 先生が言われた。そうした者は七人いる。

14.41.en: Zilu spent the night at Stone Gate. The gatekeeper said: Where are you from? Zilu said: From the house of Kong. He said: Is that the one who knows it cannot be done and still does it?
14.41.ja: 子路が石門に泊まった。門番が「どこから来た」と言うと、子路「孔氏のところからです。」門番「できないと知りながらやっている人のことか。」

14.42.en: The Master was playing the stone chimes in Wei. A man carrying a basket passed the gate of the Kong household and said: There is a heart in this playing of the chimes! After a while he said: How petty, this clanging! If no one knows you, then just stop. 'When the water is deep, wade in your clothes; when it is shallow, lift your hem.' The Master said: How decisive! There is nothing hard about that.
14.42.ja: 先生が衛で磬を打っておられた。もっこを担いで孔子の門前を通り過ぎた者が言った。「心があるな、この磬の打ち方は。」しばらくして言った。「卑しいな、かちかちと。自分を知る者がいなければ、やめればよいだけだ。深ければ衣のまま渡り、浅ければ裾をからげる。」先生「思い切りがよいな。それなら難しいことは何もない。」

14.43.en: Zizhang said: The Documents say, 'Gaozong, in the mourning hut, did not speak for three years.' What does this mean? The Master said: Why only Gaozong? The ancients were all so. When the ruler died, all the officials attended to their duties and took orders from the chief minister for three years.
14.43.ja: 子張が言った。「書に『高宗は喪に服して三年言わなかった』とあります。どういう意味ですか。」先生「高宗に限らない。昔の人はみなそうだった。君主が亡くなると、百官はそれぞれ自分の職を総べて、三年の間冢宰の命を聴いた。」

14.44.en: The Master said: When those above love ritual, the people are easy to employ.
14.44.ja: 先生が言われた。上が礼を好めば、民は使いやすい。

14.45.en: Zilu asked about the gentleman. The Master said: He cultivates himself with reverence. Is that all? He cultivates himself to bring peace to others. Is that all? He cultivates himself to bring peace to all the people. Cultivating oneself to bring peace to all the people — even Yao and Shun found this hard!
14.45.ja: 子路が君子を問うた。先生「己を修めて敬む。」「それだけですか。」「己を修めて人を安んずる。」「それだけですか。」「己を修めて百姓を安んずる。己を修めて百姓を安んずるのは、堯・舜でさえ難しいとされた。」

14.46.en: Yuan Rang sat squatting, waiting. The Master said: Young, you were not humble or respectful to elders; grown, you accomplished nothing worth mentioning; old, you do not die — you are a pest! And he tapped him on the shin with his staff.
14.46.ja: 原壌がしゃがんで待っていた。先生「若いときは謙遜も悌順もなく、長じては語るべきこともなく、老いても死なない。これこそ害だ。」杖でそのすねを叩かれた。

14.47.en: A boy from Que village was carrying messages. Someone asked about him: Is he making progress? The Master said: I see him sitting in the seat of an adult and walking side by side with his elders. He is not seeking progress; he wants to grow up fast.
14.47.ja: 闕党の童子が取り次ぎをしていた。ある人が問うた。「進歩している子ですか。」先生「彼が大人の席に座り、年長者と肩を並べて歩くのを見た。進歩を求める者ではない、早く大人になりたい者だ。」

15.1.en: Duke Ling of Wei asked Confucius about military formations. Confucius replied: Matters of sacrificial vessels I have heard about; military matters I have never studied. The next day he left. In Chen, their provisions ran out; his followers fell ill and could not rise. Zilu came to him, indignant: Does the gentleman, too, end up in straits? The Master said: The gentleman holds firm in straits; the petty man in straits loses all restraint.
15.1.ja: 衛の霊公が孔子に陣立てを問うた。孔子「祭器のことなら聞いたことがありますが、軍のことは学んでおりません。」翌日すぐに立ち去った。陳で食糧が尽き、従者は病んで起き上がれなかった。子路が怒って先生に会い言った。「君子も困窮することがあるのですか。」先生「君子はもとより窮する。小人は窮すると乱れる。」

15.2.en: The Master said: Ci, do you think I am someone who has learned a great deal and remembers it all? He replied: Yes. Is it not so? The Master said: No. I have one thread running through it all.
15.2.ja: 先生が言われた。「賜よ、お前は私が多く学んで覚えている者だと思うか。」「そうです。違うのですか。」「違う。私は一つのことで貫いている。」

15.3.en: The Master said: You, those who understand virtue are few.
15.3.ja: 先生が言われた。由よ、徳を知る者は少ない。

15.4.en: The Master said: One who governed by doing nothing — was that not Shun? What did he do? He made himself reverent and sat facing south, that was all.
15.4.ja: 先生が言われた。何もせずに治めたのは舜であろうか。何をしたか。身を恭しくして、正しく南に向いていただけだ。

15.5.en: Zizhang asked how to get along. The Master said: Let your words be loyal and true and your conduct sincere and reverent, and you will get along even among the barbarian states. If your words are not loyal and true and your conduct not sincere and reverent, will you get along even in your own neighborhood? Standing, see these before you; in your carriage, see them leaning on the crossbar. Then you will get along. Zizhang wrote this on his sash.
15.5.ja: 子張が行われることを問うた。先生「言葉が忠信で、行いが篤敬なら、蛮貊の国でも行われる。言葉が忠信でなく、行いが篤敬でなければ、郷里でも行われようか。立てばそれが目の前に並んで見え、車に乗ればそれが横木に寄りかかって見える。そうしてはじめて行われる。」子張はこれを大帯に書きつけた。

15.6.en: The Master said: How upright Shi Yu is! When the state has the Way, he is like an arrow; when the state lacks the Way, he is like an arrow. What a gentleman Qu Boyu is! When the state has the Way, he serves; when the state lacks the Way, he can roll himself up and put himself away.
15.6.ja: 先生が言われた。まっすぐだな、史魚は。国に道があっても矢のよう、道がなくても矢のようだ。君子だな、蘧伯玉は。国に道があれば仕え、道がなければ巻いて懐にしまえる。

15.7.en: The Master said: Not to speak with someone you should speak with is to lose a person; to speak with someone you should not speak with is to waste words. The wise lose neither people nor words.
15.7.ja: 先生が言われた。話すべき人と話さなければ、人を失う。話すべきでない人と話せば、言葉を失う。知者は人を失わず、言葉も失わない。

15.8.en: The Master said: A resolute scholar and a humane man will not seek to live at the expense of humaneness; they will give their lives to achieve humaneness.
15.8.ja: 先生が言われた。志士仁人は、生を求めて仁を害することはなく、身を殺して仁を成すことがある。
